h1: Right triangle side and angle Calculator
summary: The Right triangle side and angle calculator turns the side length c, the side length b and the angle β into side length a (Two sides). That makes it useful for a homework check, a spreadsheet build or a bit of mental arithmetic you want to confirm. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Right triangle side and angle calculator work?
sections.html:
The Right triangle side and angle calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports side length a (Two sides) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case; then you type in the side length c (Two sides), the side length b (Angle and one side), the angle β (Angle and one side) and the side length c (Area and one side).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Right triangle side and angle calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Side length a=the square root of (-(side length b ^ 2) + (side length c ^ 2))
Side length c=side length b ÷ the sine of (angle β)
Angle α=-angle β + (1 ÷ 2) × PI
Side length c=side length a ÷ the sine of (angle α)
Side length a=(1 ÷ 2) × the square root of (2 × (side length c ^ 2) + 2 × the square root of (-16 × (area ^ 2) + (side length c ^ 4)))
Side length a=2 × area ÷ side length b

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Length, opening in centimeters

  • Angle, opening in degrees

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Right triangle side and angle calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Settling an argument about a number with a quick, traceable result
  • Checking a homework answer before you hand it in
  • Building the same calculation into a spreadsheet and wanting a reference value
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the side length c, the side length b and the angle β — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Right triangle side and angle calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns side length a (Two sides), derived from the side length c, the side length b and the angle β. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Right triangle side and angle calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the side length c, the side length b and the angle β, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter side length a (Two sides) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Side length a (Two sides) opens in centimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Right triangle side and angle calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
